segments.text: They took his home, his family, his name, even the clothes off his back. And Frankl found the one thing the guards could never reach.
Between what happens to you and what you do next, there's a gap. And in that gap sits a freedom no one can confiscate.
He watched starving men give away their last crust of bread. Even there, how you respond stayed a choice.
You'll never face a camp. But the rule holds on any hard day: lose almost everything, and you still choose your attitude toward it.
That's Man's Search for Meaning. Honest verdict on the channel.
